Subject: Tenant data handshake & deletion SLA questions

Hi Laura,

We're finalizing our compliance checklist for the Private/VPC deployment and have a few open items about tenant data residency and deletion that legal and security need clarified before we sign the SOW. Quick list so we can consolidate answers: 

- Since storage is customer-controlled (our S3 buckets in the VPC), what exactly does Redwood delete versus what we as the customer must delete?
- Is there a recommended canonical deletion handshake (API call + confirmations) so Aurora can automate the final wipe?
- How long after a deletion trigger can we expect objects/replicas and metadata to be gone (object storage and any infra-level snapshots)?
- Can Redwood provide a signed attestation/certificate that documents the deletion workflow and timestamps?
- What evidence (audit logs, checksums, object manifests) will you be able to provide for regulatory audit?

Please include any limitations (e.g., dependent on cloud provider retention, eventual consistency) so we can scope our controls. Can we get a short write-up by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks — Priya
Priya Desai
Head of IT Compliance, Aurora Health Systems

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Tenant data handshake & deletion SLA questions

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers up front, followed by concrete next steps.

Summary answers:
- Ownership: In the Private/VPC model where storage is customer-managed, the object data itself remains in your S3 buckets; Redwood never migrates custody to our hosted storage. Redwood manages runtime artifacts (KV caches, ephemeral replicas on compute nodes) and the control-plane metadata.
- Deletion handshake: We support a 2-step deletion handshake we recommend you implement: (1) Customer issues a DeleteTenant API call (or marks tenant in your orchestration) that triggers Redwood's orchestration to start deprovisioning; (2) Redwood returns a signed acknowledgement with a deletion-ticket ID and a checklist of background jobs kicked off. Once background jobs complete, Redwood responds with a final signed confirmation.
- Timing: For ephemeral runtime caches and control-plane metadata we remove pointers immediately; purging of objects in your S3 is driven by your lifecycle policies — typical final object disappearance is 24–72 hours depending on replication and provider GC. Snapshots/backups are subject to your snapshot retention policy; we recommend short retention windows for tenant-scoped snapshots if fast irrevocable deletion is required.
- Attestation: Yes — we can produce a signed attestation (PDF) that records the deletion-ticket ID, timestamps of orchestration events, and hashes of manifests we processed. We cannot, however, cause your cloud provider to expunge copies held by their replication windows — we will document that limitation.
- Evidence: We can provide: signed orchestration logs, control-plane audit trail (events + event hashes), and an object manifest (filenames/keys + checksums) that we processed during the purge.

Next steps I propose:
1) Tech call tomorrow with Karthik (in infra) and your DevOps to map the DeleteTenant API to your orchestration.
2) Redwood operations will create a deletion attestation template for legal to review (we can iterate).
3) If you want stronger guarantees we can recommend a lifecycle configuration and a short snapshot retention window; we can also run a dry-run and provide logs.

Can you do 11 AM PT tomorrow for the call? If yes, I'll loop in Monica from CS to own scheduling and the post-call artifacts.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Exec — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

Hi Priya — adding some operational detail from Infra that will help your SREs design automation. Quoting Laura's summary above for context.

Operational details (for automation):
- Delete flow outline:
  1) Customer triggers DeleteTenant (API or orchestration flag).
  2) Redwood control-plane marks tenant state = DELETING and emits DeletionRequested event with deletion-ticket id.
  3) Runtime fleet drains new requests for the tenant, KV caches are invalidated; ephemeral caches are cleared within the first orchestration window (minutes).
  4) Background workers reconcile and mark object keys processed. We push an object-manifest (key list + checksum) to your S3 location (or a signed manifest if you prefer us to write to a pre-agreed bucket path).
  5) Redwood emits DeletionComplete and returns a signed confirmation (includes event hashes).

- Timelines and caveats:
  - Control-plane metadata removal and cache invalidation: immediate (seconds–minutes).
  - Runtime ephemeral remnants (local disk on compute nodes): generally cleared in the same orchestration window, but you should account for 1–3 hours for node recycling in large fleets.
  - Customer object deletion: Redwood cannot delete objects from customer-managed buckets without a delegated role/policy. If you give Redwood a short-lived delete role we can execute deletions on your behalf and report completion. Otherwise we provide the manifest and orchestration timestamps and you confirm deletion on your side.
  - Snapshots: if you use provider-managed snapshots, deletion follows your snapshot lifecycle; snapshots can create out-of-band copies — please configure short retention if regulatory erasure is required.

- Evidence we can provide programmatically:
  - Signed orchestration events stream (JSON lines) with event hashes
  - Manifest file (keys + checksums) we processed and optionally signed by our HSM
  - Time-stamped audit records we can push to your secure bucket (read-only to Redwood)

I attached a simple visual "delete-path-sequence.png" showing the orchestration steps and an S3 lifecycle example (s3-lifecycle-example.txt) you can drop into your IaC.

If Aurora wants Redwood to perform the final object deletion, we will require a narrowly scoped IAM role and an execution window; that enables us to produce an end-to-end attestation where we also sign that objects were removed. Without that role, attestation will state the orchestration and manifest generation happened but final object disappearance must be verified by Aurora's lifecycle.

Happy to walk through these points on the call; Laura, Monica — can we confirm 11 AM PT?

— Karthik
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

Regards,
